questions.question: What does Ada like to do when she is little and doesn’t talk yet? (Look at how she explores and looks at things.)
questions.explanation: This helps children notice Ada’s curiosity, even before she talks, and understand that exploring is part of learning.

questions.question: How do Ada’s parents feel when she starts asking lots of questions? Why do they still encourage her?
questions.explanation: Reflecting on the parents’ feelings helps children see that curiosity might surprise adults, but asking questions is good.

questions.question: Ada asks many 'Why?' and 'How?' questions. Can you share a question you asked when you were curious about something?
questions.explanation: Connecting Ada’s questions to their own helps children relate the moral to their real life, encouraging curiosity.

questions.question: Ada’s experiments sometimes make a mess at home and at school. Why is making a mess or mistake okay when you are learning something new?
questions.explanation: This encourages kids to see that mistakes are part of learning, an important part of the story’s moral.

questions.question: What did Ada do when she couldn’t figure out where the bad smell was coming from? Did she give up?
questions.explanation: Understanding that Ada kept trying shows perseverance, linking to the story’s lesson about always being curious and not giving up.

questions.question: How do Ada’s parents act when they get frustrated by her curiosity? What changes later?
questions.explanation: Talking about the parents' change helps children see that adults can learn to support curiosity, too.

questions.question: Can you think of a time you tried to learn something new and made a little mess or mistake? What did you do next?
questions.explanation: This lets children connect their experiences to Ada’s, reinforcing that learning is sometimes messy and that’s okay.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep asking questions, even if you don’t know the answer right away?
questions.explanation: This question helps children understand the value of not giving up and always being curious, which is the core of the moral.

questions.question: What are some things you would like to learn more about? How can asking questions help you?
questions.explanation: It encourages children to think about their own interests and how curiosity can help them grow and learn.

questions.question: How does Ada feel when she sits in the Thinking Chair? What helps her start feeling better?
questions.explanation: This helps kids understand feelings about making mistakes and how curiosity can turn a sad moment into a learning moment.

moral: It's okay to be curious and ask lots of questions. Learning and discovering new things is wonderful, and making mistakes or messes is part of how we learn. Always be curious and keep trying, just like Ada!
learning_objectives: Children will identify ways to be curious and ask questions about the world.
Children will understand that making mistakes and messes is a normal part of learning.
Children will practice sharing their own experiences with curiosity and learning.
Children will learn how to support others’ curiosity and learning, just like Ada’s family.
